note: Free sources only, usable in commercial work. quality is a judgement (1-5) from published models and features, not from test renders. live: the list is read from the source at search time (umd characters). Licences are recorded per downloaded file in .motion/assets.lock.json.

entries.name: Rain v3 (Blender Studio)
entries.animations: none; pose library and rig UI included
entries.licence: CC BY 4.0
entries.blender: 4.1 and later (page). Tested on 5.1.2 with scripts disabled (2026-11-11): opens and renders with its textures, profile complete (CloudRig family, nothing missing), head turn, blink, jaw speech and breathing work; its 752 drivers are simple expressions and run without scripts. Eye aim is exact with the head still; with the head turned, the iris follows the rig's own EyeDot system and is not solved yet: check the eyes in the test shot
entries.use: Hero close-ups and acting: eye, eyelid, mouth and brow controls, corrective shapes.
entries.caution: Do not name the character or its film in an advert; logos of the Blender Foundation are excluded from the licence.

entries.name: Snow v4 (Blender Studio)
entries.licence: CC BY 4.0
entries.use: Second hero for dialogue between two characters.
entries.caution: Same as Rain.

entries.name: Spring (Blender Studio)
entries.licence: CC BY 4.0
entries.blender: 2.8 to 3.6 announced: test under your version before planning a shot
entries.use: The only film-grade free child character found.
entries.caution: Old rig: may break on Blender 4.x and 5.x.

entries.name: Blender Studio character library
entries.licence: CC BY 4.0 (check each page)
entries.use: More film characters and creatures; each has its own rig and Blender version.
entries.caution: Some downloads need a Blender Studio subscription: then it is not free, skip it.

entries.name: MPFB2 (MakeHuman for Blender)
entries.licence: code GPL-3.0; core assets CC0; extra packs CC0 or CC BY (check each)
entries.redistribute: yes (characters made of core assets only)

get.install: Blender > Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions > search MPFB

entries.use: Families and casts: age, weight, muscle, proportions by script (HumanService.create_human), batch variations for a crowd or a family; visemes02 pack gives 15 mouth shapes.
entries.caution: Game-like realism; hair as cards. Packs from third parties carry their own licence.

entries.name: MPFB MCP server
entries.licence: GPL-3.0
entries.use: Optional, for exploring a character live in an open Blender (42 tools, beta). Batch renders use MPFB from Python instead.
entries.caution: Beta.

entries.name: KayKit Adventurers
entries.use: Barbarian, Knight, Mage, Rogue: animated from the first minute, for a demo or a playful spot.
entries.caution: Painted faces: no lip sync.

entries.name: KayKit Skeletons
entries.use: Mage, Minion, Rogue, Warrior skeletons: Halloween, games, humour.

entries.name: Mesh2Motion rigs (human and animals)
entries.animations: about 330 clips (human 234, fox 21, horse 14, dragon 12, spider 11, kaiju 10, bird 9, snake 8, shark 7)
entries.licence: CC0 1.0 (assets); code MIT
entries.use: Animals and creatures with their own animations; a large human clip library to retarget on any humanoid.
entries.caution: Some human clips are tagged quaternius: their source licence is recorded as given.

entries.name: 100Avatars R1 to R3 (Polygonal Mind)
entries.animations: none; humanoid, so any humanoid clip retargets
entries.licence: CC0 1.0 (Open Source Avatars registry)
entries.use: 300 varied characters (people, animals, objects with faces, robots), each with a voxel twin, visemes for speech; enough for a crowd or a cast.
entries.caution: The authors ask not to sell the avatars themselves without major changes: using them in a video is fine.

entries.name: Open Source Avatars collections
entries.licence: CC0 or CC BY per collection
entries.use: Thousands of VRM avatars (chibis, Halloween, heroes) with a licence stated per collection.
entries.caution: Files are served from IPFS or Arweave: a download can be slow.

entries.name: VRoid Studio sample models D to G
entries.licence: CC0 for samples D to G; A to C have their own terms

get.how: Download in VRoid Studio or VRoid Hub, export as VRM, then umd characters add <file> --id vroid-samples

entries.use: Anime characters with face expressions and mouth shapes (A I U E O).
entries.caution: Import needs the VRM add-on for Blender.

entries.name: VRoid Studio (make your own anime character)
entries.licence: free software; presets are not CC0 but may be used commercially, videos that earn money included

get.how: Make the character in VRoid Studio (no API), export VRM, then umd characters add

entries.use: A custom anime mascot designed by the user in minutes, sliders only.
entries.caution: Pixiv forbids building an app that generates avatars from its assets: the plugin imports finished characters, never generates them.

entries.name: Quaternius characters (Universal Base Characters and other packs)
entries.licence: QAL v1.0 since 2026-08-28 (use, modify and sell products; no resale of the assets themselves); earlier downloads stay CC0

get.how: Download the free Standard pack, then umd characters add <file> --id quaternius-characters

entries.use: Six body types (Regular, Superhero, Teen), 20 haircuts; many more packs: animals, monsters, robots, modular people.
entries.caution: Keep the asset files out of public repositories.

entries.name: Kenney animated characters (Protagonists, Retro, Mini, Blocky)
entries.animations: basic set in the animated packs

get.how: Download the zip from the page (also: animated-characters-protagonists, animated-characters-retro, blocky-characters), then umd characters add

entries.use: Toy-like casts, game looks, quick prototypes.

entries.name: CharMorph (Vitruvian CC0, Antonia CC BY)
entries.licence: add-on GPL-3.0; Vitruvian base CC0; Antonia and Reom CC BY; MB-Lab bases AGPL (excluded)
entries.credit: Antonia or Reom: their authors (CC BY)
entries.redistribute: Vitruvian yes; Antonia and Reom with credit

get.how: Install the add-on, pick the Vitruvian, Antonia or Reom base, never the MB-Lab ones

entries.blender: last release about March 2025: test on your version
entries.use: Realistic adults with a full Rigify face rig.
entries.caution: Bases from MB-Lab are AGPL: refused for client work.

entries.name: Blender Human Base Meshes
entries.licence: CC0 according to the research notes; check the bundle's own licence file

get.how: Download the Human Base Meshes bundle, sculpt, then rig with the Rigify human metarig

entries.use: The start for a custom stylised character (a mascot of the brand), sculpted then rigged.
entries.caution: Not rigged, no textures: a modelling job, not a ready character.

entries.name: Rigify human metarig on your own mesh
entries.licence: GPL (ships with Blender); the rig you generate is yours

get.install: Built into Blender 4.2 and later: enable Rigify in Preferences > Add-ons

entries.use: Rig any humanoid mesh (Human Base Meshes, a sculpt, a CC0 model without bones) with body and face controls.

entries.name: Anny (NAVER LABS) parametric body
entries.licence: Apache-2.0; data CC0 (except the optional SMPL-X topology, non-commercial)
entries.use: Advanced: body shapes from infant to senior generated in Python, exported to Blender.
entries.caution: No Blender integration; never enable the SMPL-X option.

entries.name: Sketchfab downloadable models (CC0 and CC BY only)
entries.licence: per model: keep only CC0 and CC BY; refuse NC, ND, SA and Editorial

get.how: The user downloads (free account), then umd characters add <file> --id sketchfab-cc --licence "CC BY 4.0" --author name --url page

entries.use: The widest choice: thousands of rigged characters; filter on CC0 and CC BY (link above).
entries.caution: Quality and rig vary widely: check the rig before planning. Never models of real people or brands.

entries.name: Poly Pizza (low-poly models, CC0 and CC BY)
entries.licence: per model (Creative Commons licence at download time)

get.how: Download by hand (the terms forbid automated downloads), then umd characters add

entries.use: Props and simple characters to fill a low-poly world.
entries.caution: No scripted downloads.

entries.name: OpenGameArt 3D characters (CC0 and CC BY only)
entries.licence: per asset: keep CC0 and CC BY; refuse GPL art, CC BY-SA and OGA-BY for client work unless the user accepts

get.how: Download by hand, then umd characters add

entries.use: Game characters, monsters, retro looks.

entries.name: Mesh2Motion animation clips
entries.animations: about 330 clips, one GLB each (walk, run, idle, emotes, attacks, sit, dance…)
entries.use: Body motion for any humanoid through the canonical bone map (character.py retarget).

entries.name: Quaternius Universal Animation Library 1 and 2
entries.licence: QAL v1.0 for new downloads (use in products allowed, no resale of the files)

get.how: Download UAL 1 or 2 (also universalanimationlibrary2.html), then umd characters add

entries.use: Named actions for stylised humanoids.

entries.name: CMU motion capture (BVH conversion)
entries.animations: about 2,500 captures: walks, sports, dances, gestures, interactions
entries.licence: free for research and commercial projects; do not resell the data itself; acknowledgement asked
entries.credit: The data used in this project was obtained from mocap.cs.cmu.edu.

get.how: Pick a clip from the index, download the .bvh, then umd characters add <file> --id cmu-mocap

entries.use: Real human motion; retarget with character.py.
entries.caution: 120 fps with a T-pose at frame 0; fingers carry no data.

entries.name: 100STYLE locomotion dataset
entries.animations: 100 walking styles (proud, sneaky, old, robot, zombie…), 60 fps
entries.licence: CC BY 4.0
entries.use: A walk with character: 100 named styles.
entries.caution: 1.5 GB archive; clips start and end in T-pose (trim with Frame_Cuts.csv).

entries.name: Open Peeps (Pablo Stanley)
entries.animations: none; animate parts in the 2D puppet

get.how: Download the library (free) or single SVGs, then umd characters add

entries.use: Hand-drawn people for explainers: mix faces, hair, bodies; split into puppet parts.

entries.name: Humaaans (Pablo Stanley)

get.how: Download the library, then umd characters add

entries.use: Flat corporate people for product and SaaS videos.
entries.caution: Seen everywhere: add your own palette to avoid the generic look.

entries.name: DiceBear avatar styles (generated from a seed)
entries.licence: library MIT; styles: 42 CC0 (lorelei, notionists, open-peeps, thumbs, pixel-art…), 14 CC BY 4.0 (adventurer, micah, personas, big-smile…), avataaars and bottts free for commercial use
entries.credit: CC BY styles: their artist (see the licence page)

get.install: npm install @dicebear/core @dicebear/styles in the project, then new Avatar(style, { seed }).toString()

entries.use: Dozens of consistent faces from seeds: a crowd, a user list, a leaderboard, quiz players.
entries.caution: The public HTTP API is for non-commercial use only: generate locally for client work.

entries.name: Kenney 2D characters (Toon Characters and others)

get.how: Download the zip, then umd characters add

entries.use: Game-style 2D characters with poses (270 files in Toon Characters 1).

entries.name: LottieFiles free animations (Lottie Simple License)
entries.licence: Lottie Simple License: commercial use and changes allowed, no attribution needed; redistribution keeps the same terms

get.how: Download the Lottie JSON, then umd characters add <file> --id lottie-community --author name --url page

entries.use: Ready animated characters for UI, explainers and stickers.
entries.caution: Check that the file is listed as free; never compile files to rebuild a similar service.

entries.name: Rive community files (CC BY)
entries.licence: per file (many CC BY); runtimes MIT

get.how: Download a remixable CC BY file, then umd characters add

entries.use: Interactive mascots with bones and facial states, rendered by the MIT web runtime.
entries.caution: The Rive editor's video export is paid: render through the web runtime and umd capture instead.

entries.name: Grease Pencil v3 (2D drawn rig in Blender)
entries.licence: part of Blender (GPL); drawings are yours
entries.use: 2D characters in a 3D scene, scriptable (drawing.add_strokes, Armature modifier), rendered by EEVEE.
entries.caution: Importing SVG into Grease Pencil under 5.x is not verified.

entries.name: COA Tools 2 (cut-out sprites in Blender)
entries.licence: GPL-3.0

get.how: Install the add-on, import a layered PSD, Krita or GIMP drawing

entries.use: A drawn character split in layers, animated with bones like Spine, for free.

entries.name: UMD 2D puppet (code)
entries.animations: blink, look, breathe, gestures, mouth shapes from umd lipsync
entries.licence: MIT (this plugin)
entries.use: A cut-out character driven on the virtual clock: works with your own drawing, Open Peeps parts or DiceBear faces.
entries.caution: Quality depends on the drawing; give each part its own pivot.

entries.name: Rhubarb Lip Sync
entries.animations: mouth cues from a voice recording (A to H, X)
entries.licence: MIT; the lip-sync data belongs to you

get.install: umd doctor --fix --rhubarb (official release, about 85 MB) or set UMD_RHUBARB to the executable

entries.use: umd lipsync voice.wav --text script.txt: mouth shapes per frame for character.py and the 2D puppet.
entries.caution: The default recogniser is English only; for French, use the phonetic recogniser (automatic when the project language is not English).

entries.name: VRM Add-on for Blender
entries.licence: MIT and GPL-3.0
entries.use: Imports .vrm (100Avatars, VRoid, Open Source Avatars) by script: bpy.ops.import_scene.vrm(filepath=...).

entries.name: Character built from primitives (three.js or Blender, code)
entries.licence: yours
entries.use: Robots, blobs, objects with eyes: shapes that do not need human acting.
entries.caution: Human faces and hands made in code look stiff: prefer an entry above for people.

excluded.name: Mixamo characters and animations
excluded.why: raw files may not be redistributed, even for free

excluded.name: Bandai Namco Research motion dataset, LAFAN1, SFU mocap
Liberated Pixel Cup sprites
excluded.why: CC BY-SA and GPL art: share-alike

excluded.why: paid, and their content may not be redistributed

excluded.name: MetaHuman
excluded.why: Epic licence: files may not be redistributed; use only if the user already works with it

excluded.name: Meshy, Tripo, Rodin, Hunyuan3D and other generated 3D
